result:
I don't know of a single Google document that prescribes an official alert list and output format for this setup, and I'd rather not invent one. What follows is what I know of Google's building blocks, plus a reasonable alert set built from them. Check the details against the current Cloud Run, Cloud Monitoring and Google Cloud Observability docs, because the GenAI parts change quickly.

## Output format
- **Alerting policies** are Cloud Monitoring resources. You can define them as JSON or YAML and create them with `gcloud monitoring policies create --policy-from-file=...` (it was under `gcloud alpha` for a long time, so check your version).
- **Terraform** (`google_monitoring_alert_policy`) is the other common route.
- Each policy has conditions, which are either metric threshold conditions (MQL or PromQL) or log-match conditions. It also has notification channels, a documentation block, and optionally a duration and auto-close.
- If your agent exports OTLP metrics to Google Cloud, they arrive as Prometheus-style custom or `prometheus.googleapis.com` metrics. PromQL-based conditions then work well.

## Suggested alerts

**Latency**
- Cloud Run built-in `run.googleapis.com/request_latencies`: alert on p95 or p99 above your SLO for several minutes.
- OTel GenAI metric `gen_ai.client.operation.duration`: alert on slow model calls or tool calls.
- Time to first token, if you stream.

**Errors**
- Cloud Run `request_count` filtered to `response_code_class="5xx"`, as a ratio of all requests.
- Container crashes, startup failures and OOM kills, from logs or `container/memory/utilizations`.
- Agent-level failure rates from OTel spans or metrics, such as tool errors, model API errors and rate limiting (429s).

**Cost**
- There is no native "dollar" metric for model usage.
- Alert on `gen_ai.client.token.usage` (input and output tokens) rising abnormally versus a baseline, for example a rate-of-change or anomaly alert. This catches runaway loops.
- Use a Cloud Billing budget for actual spend, since budgets have their own alert mechanism.
- Alert on Cloud Run instance count or CPU for infrastructure cost.

**Safety**
- Google doesn't give you a ready-made safety metric for custom agents.
- Alert on log-based metrics for blocked or flagged responses, such as Vertex AI safety-filter finish reasons and Model Armor findings (prompt injection, jailbreak, sensitive data).
- Alert on a spike in guardrail triggers.

**Quality**
- This is the hardest to alert on in real time.
- Run evaluations (for example the Vertex AI Gen AI evaluation service, or LLM-as-judge on sampled traces). Emit the scores as custom metrics, then alert on a drop below a threshold.
- Proxy signals include tool-call failure rates, retry counts, excessive agent steps and user feedback.

## Caveats
- The OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions are still experimental. Metric and attribute names may change, so pin versions and check names before writing alert queries.
- Capturing prompt and response content is opt-in. It has privacy and PII implications and adds log volume and cost.
- Avoid high-cardinality labels such as user IDs or full prompts in metrics.
- Cloud Run metrics are sampled and delayed, so use sensible alignment periods and durations to avoid flapping.
- Token counts are only a proxy for cost, because pricing differs by model and by input versus output.
- Quality and safety alerts depend on evaluation pipelines you must build, so they won't work out of the box.
- Instrumentation is only as good as what the agent framework emits. Some frameworks, such as ADK, emit GenAI spans and metrics natively, and others need extra instrumentation.

If you want, I can draft example policy files in YAML or Terraform.
